Create Age Group Labels for a Reporting Tree

Source: R/age_labels_tree.R
age_labels_tree.Rd

Create labels for a reporting tree, in which records are tabulated at different levels of detail: detailed age groups, broader age groups, and, optionally, age not stated.

Usage

age_labels_tree(
  breaks,
  nodes = NULL,
  open_right = TRUE,
  include_missing = TRUE
)

Arguments

breaks

Boundaries between age groups. A numeric vector.

nodes

Labels for broad age groups. A character vector, or NULL (the default), in which case there are no broad age groups.

open_right

Whether the oldest age group is open on the right, i.e. has no upper limit. Default is TRUE.

include_missing

Whether to include a "Missing" category, representing age not stated. Default is TRUE.

Value

Character vector.

Details

The most detailed age groups (the leaves of the tree) are created from breaks and open_right, exactly as by age_labels(). Broader age groups are supplied through nodes, as ordinary age group labels such as "0-14" or "65+". Broader age groups can be given in any order, and can nest to any depth: for instance, nodes = c("0-14", "15+", "15-64", "65+") describes a tree where "15+" is divided into "15-64" and "65+", each of which is divided into detailed age groups. Leaves do not need to be the same distance from the root.

Each broad age group must start and end at values in breaks (or be open, if open_right is TRUE), so that it is a union of detailed age groups. It must contain at least two detailed age groups, but not all of them, and broad age groups must nest: any two either do not overlap, or one contains the other. Labels in nodes are converted to the standard format used by age_standard(), so that, for instance, "Under 15" becomes "0-14".

The root of the tree, representing records with no information on age, is labelled "Missing". Unlike age_labels(), age_labels_tree() includes "Missing" by default, since most reporting trees in practice have a category for age not stated.

Labels are returned in the same order as age_set_order_tree(): detailed age groups, then broad age groups (each after the age groups inside it), then "Missing".

See also

  • age_labels() Create labels without broad age groups

  • age_set_order_tree() Order existing labels as a tree

  • age_diagnose_values() Check labels, including with valid_tree = TRUE

  • period_labels_tree() Period equivalent of age_labels_tree()

  • cohort_labels_tree() Cohort equivalent of age_labels_tree()

Examples

## census with 5-year and 10-year age groups,
## age reported only as under or over 15,
## and age not stated
age_labels_tree(
  breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, seq(20, 70, 10)),
  nodes = c("0-14", "15+")
)
#>  [1] "0-4"     "5-9"     "10-14"   "15-19"   "20-29"   "30-39"   "40-49"  
#>  [8] "50-59"   "60-69"   "70+"     "0-14"    "15+"     "Missing"

## three levels, with leaves at different depths
age_labels_tree(
  breaks = seq(0, 85, 5),
  nodes = c("0-14", "15+", "15-64", "65+")
)
#>  [1] "0-4"     "5-9"     "10-14"   "15-19"   "20-24"   "25-29"   "30-34"  
#>  [8] "35-39"   "40-44"   "45-49"   "50-54"   "55-59"   "60-64"   "65-69"  
#> [15] "70-74"   "75-79"   "80-84"   "85+"     "0-14"    "15-64"   "65+"    
#> [22] "15+"     "Missing"

## no broad age groups, no "Missing"
age_labels_tree(
  breaks = seq(0, 20, 5),
  include_missing = FALSE
)
#> [1] "0-4"   "5-9"   "10-14" "15-19" "20+"
